Isaac (knee) is out for Friday's game in Toronto.

Penda was diagnosed with a partially torn right hamstring Saturday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
Suggs has been diagnosed with a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.

BOS.note: Carter has been diagnosed with mononucleosis and is without a timetable for a return, Gary Washburn of The Boston Globe reports.

IND.note: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least the next two weeks of action, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
McConnell (hamstring) is practicing in the G League at Noblesville Boom training camp, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
Zubac (ankle) will remain on the inactive list for Sunday's game against the Nets.

BKN.note: Bilodeau (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
Brown (rest) is out for Sunday's game in Indiana.
The Nets exercised Demin's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.

GS.note: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
Curry (rest) won't play Sunday against the Clippers, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.

Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
The Warriors are exploring potential trades involving Porzingis (personal), who remains away from the team indefinitely while dealing with ongoing health concerns, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.

Strus (foot) is making progress but is set to miss at least one more week, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.

LAL.note: Thiero (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors.

Leonard (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least three to four weeks, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
